notes: as in "an isaac run", a single playthrough of a arcade/rogulike game
split into parts so that we can provide examples alongside text easily
en:
[b]Mahjong Fundamentals[/b]
Every round, the basic aim is to build a winning hand with the 13 tiles in hand combined with a final 14th tile. This last tile is either drawn yourself or discarded by an opponent player.
Wtih two exceptions (Chiitoitsu and Kokushi Musou), every hand is made up of 3 groups of 3 and a pair of 2. Groups are either runs in a suit of length 3, sets of identical tiles of size 3, or sets of size 4 (which trigger an additional draw, so that the rest of the hand still completes naturally). An example hand is given below:

This hand consists of a run of 123-Pin, a run of 234-Sou and of 678-Sou, a pair of 9-Man, and a set of Red Dragons, totalling, once more, to 4 groups and a pair.
Critically, this hand meets at least one win condition, more commonly referred to as [i]Yaku[/i]. Here, the hand meets [i]Yakuhai[/i] by having a set of Red Dragons. A hand [i]is not valid[/i] if it does not meet at least one Yaku. Refer to the Yaku tab for information on specific Yaku, but Yakuhai is one of the more easily acheivable ones (which have been starred for reference). Riichi is perhaps the most critical to understand, but the explanation behind it is left in the Yaku tab.
A round ends when the number of tiles left in the wall reaches a cutoff, 30 by default. If you have not gone out by this point, you get no points.

[b]UltiMahjong Fundamentals[/b]
The whole game is played out across 16 rounds. Every round, your seat wind advances in counterclockwise compass order (N>W>S>E), and every four rounds, the prevalent wind advances in clockwise compass order (E>S>W>N).
At the end of every round, you must have met a minimum score to continue the run. This minimum threshold increases every round. The amount that it will increase next round also increases.
Finishing a round opens the shop, and grants you a static amount of money. You can buy anything you have enough money for, or sell items for money. All unspent money is [i]forfeited[/i] when you close the shop!
Terminal: 1 or 9 in any number suit.
Simple: 2 through 8 in any number suit.
Yakuhai: Dragons and the sitting and prevalent winds (bottom left corner).
ja: 役牌：元牌と場風と自風。

en: Flowers: Not always included, indicated by a number in the top left. Worth bonus han if called. Calling them immediately draws a replacement tile.
ja: 花牌：普通に利用していない。ドラを得る。

en: Pair: 2 tiles of the same value and suit.
Set: 3 tiles of the same value and suit.

Quad: 4 tiles of the same value and suit. [i]Must[/i] be called to count, this call's name is kan. Calling kan draws another tile into hand, so quads are effectively still sets of size 3, but with a bonus tile tacked on for extra fu. Calling kan also reveals another kan dora.
Run: 3 tiles in a row of the same number suit. Individual runs can [i]only[/i] be 3 tiles long.
ja: 順子：連続する三枚の牌。

en: Some tiles are worth 1 han just for being in hand at completion. However, you still need to have at least one Yaku in hand to go out. They are as follows:
ja: ある牌は手配に存在するだけで翻を得る。だが、ドラだけで和了できない、まだ役が必要だ。

en: Kan: Every time a kan is called, a tile is revealed from the dead wall. The tile following it in sequence becomes a bonus tile. For number tiles, the order is sequential (1...9>1). For dragons, the order is W>G>R>W. For Winds: N>E>S>W>N.

These are the basic waits formally recognized in Riichi Mahjong. All waits award 2 fu if used as the final wait except Ryanmen, which awards 0. (More complex waits exist, but can be always broken down into a combination of these basic ones, although I leave discovering them as an exercise for the reader.)
They are ordered here by approximate likelihood of completion (in a vacuum).

notes: i wouldn't translate the names for these wait terms, just leave them as is. even in normal english "ryanmen" or "tanki" are accepted, no need to invent vocab
en: Ryanmen: Often translated as "two-sided," this is two adjacent tiles waiting for a third to complete a run from either end.
Shanpon: Two pairs waiting for one to resolve to a set.
Penchan and Kanchan: Like Ryanmen, waits on a run to complete, but because of shape or terminality, only waits on one tile instead of two.

Tanki: A single tile waits on a copy of itself to complete a pair. Note the common complex wait pattern Nobetan (e.g. 3456) [i]still counts[/i] as a Tanki wait, even though you are technically waiting on two tiles.

Before we begin, the scoring used here is [i]not the same[/i] as in normal Riichi, although it approximates it fairly closely. (If you already understand Riichi scoring, you should just know: Ron and Tsumo now award the same amount of points, 10 Fu is now worth 400 points exactly instead of ~300, Fu are rounded [i]down[/i] to the nearest 10, and Mangan rounding is smoothed so that more Han always equate to more points earned.)

A hand [i]demands[/i] at least 1 Han and scores 1000 points by default. There are two fundamental factors to inproving this score: Fu and more Han.

Fu are awarded for completing sets and for riskier waits, among other factors. See the "Fu" tab. Every 10 fu rounded [i]down[/i] awards 400 more points.

Han, also known as "doublers," are the more significant factor. All Yaku award some number of Han, and again, you need at least 1. Every additional han doubles the basic score of {1000+fu points}. For example, a 3 Han hand without significant fu is worth {1000×2×2} = 4000 points. A 2 Han hand with 10 fu is worth {1400×2} = 2800 points.
(It may be easier to think of the basic score as {500+200 per 10 Fu}, and the first Han as a doubler as well.)

Once you exceed 8000 points, Fu are no longer counted, and the score rewarded is simply the number of Han multiplied by 2000. After you exceed 10 Han, every additional Han is worth 4000 more points, up to the Yakuman Limit at 13 Han = 32000 points.

Sitting in the East seat multiplies the final value by 1.5. For example, the minimum scoring hand in the East seat is 1500, and a Yakuman is 48000 points.

en: Declare Riichi with your first discard.
Win before or on your first draw after declaring Rīchi.
ja: 立直した後、牌を捨てる前に上がる。

en: Win off the last drawn tile in the wall.
ja: 牌山の最後の牌で上がる。

en: Win off the tile redraw when calling a kan.
ja: カンした後の牌で上がる。

en: Win by tsumo with a closed hand.
ja: 門前のまま自摸で上がる。

en: Hand contains seven pairs. Four of the same tile [i]does not count[/i] as two pairs, they [i]must[/i] all be unique.
A round ends with no other win, and your [i]discards[/i] consist solely of terminals and honors.
ja: 上がらなくて局を終えて、自分の捨牌は幺九牌だけだった。

en: No fu except futei and dora fu. This works out to mean: All runs, non-yakuhai pair, and a ryanmen wait.
ja: 符を得ない。つまり、頭が役牌でない、順子だけの両面待ち。

en: Two copies of the same run.
Two copies of Iipeikou. The two Iipeikou [i]may[/i] be of different suits, or they [i]may[/i] contain duplicate tiles. [i]Incompatible[/i] with Chiitoitsu.
The same value run in three numbered suits.
ja: 三種類の数牌に同じ順子。
サンショクドージュン

en: 1-9 in a single suit. [i]Specifically demands[/i] a winning hand containing the runs 123, 456, and 789, [i]not[/i] just having at least one of every tile.
ja: ある数牌の種類の１～９。厳密に、１２３と４５６と７８９の順子が必要。

en: Hand consists of four set/quads and a pair.
ja: 頭一つ、残りの面子が刻子や槓子。

en: Three concealed sets/quads. The [i]sets themselves[/i] must be entirely concealed; finishing the last set with ron does [i]not[/i] qualify.

ja: 三回カンを鳴く。暗槓でも明槓でもいい。

en: The same value set in three numbered suits.
ja: 三種類の数牌に同じ刻子や槓子。

en: Called flower tile. Does [i]not[/i] contribute to the one Han minimum required to go out.
ja: 花。厳密に、ドラだ。花牌で一翻縛りを越えない。

en: No terminals or honors in hand.
ja: 字牌と数牌の１と９がない。
タンヤオ、タンヤオチュー

en: Set or quad of seat wind, prevalent wind, or any dragon. Stacks with self if multiple qualifying sets are present.
ja: 元牌、または場風や自風。

en: Two Dragon sets/quads and a Dragon pair. Adds onto the existing two Yakuhai, for four total han awarded on the dragons.
ja: 元牌の刻子や槓子二つ、対子一つ。

en: Every grouping/pair contains an honor or terminal.
ja: 全部の面子が字牌や老頭牌を含む。
チャンタ、ホンチャンタイヤオチュウ

en: Every grouping/pair contains a terminal. Disables Chanta.
ja: 全部の面子が老頭を含む。
ジュンチャン、ジュンチャンタイヤオチュウ

en: Every grouping is composed entirely of terminals or honors. Additonally implies either Toitoi or Chiitoitsu, for at least four han. Disables Junchan and Chanta.
ja: 全部の牌が字牌や老頭牌。七対子か対々和はおろか。

en: Hand only contains honors and tiles of a single suit.
ja: ある数牌の種類と字牌だけ。

en: Hand only contains tiles of a single suit.

Note that Yakuman are automatic limit hands. That is, once you acheive [i]at least[/i] one Yakuman, the score rewarded is simply 32000 (48000 if sitting East) multiplied by the number of fulfilled Yakuman.

Never awarded itself, simply a name for any hand that reaches or exceeds thirteen han without fulfilling any defined Yakuman pattern. Any other Yakuman disables this one, so there can be no multiple Yakuman hands containing Kazoe.
ja: ちゃんとした役満じゃない、ほかの役満なしで十三翻を超えると数え役満になる。
元牌の刻子や槓子三つ。

en: Three sets/quads of winds and a pair of the fourth.
ja: 風牌の刻子や槓子三つ、対子一つ。
風牌の刻子や槓子四つ。

en: Four concealed sets/quads. The [i]sets themselves[/i] must be entirely concealed; finishing the last set with ron does [i]not[/i] qualify.

ja: 四回カンを鳴く。暗槓でも明槓でもいい。

en: One of every terminal and honor, and a second of any of them.
ja: 字牌や老頭牌から、十二枚複数のない牌と一つの対子。

en: Hand only contains 2/3/4/6/8-Sou and Green Dragons. These are traditionally the tiles with only green ink on them, however, recolored variants of these tiles still contribute.
1112345678999 of any suit, plus one more tile from the suit.
ja: ある数牌の種類の１１１２３４５６７８９９９とその種類から何でももう一つ。

ja: 牌を捨てなくて上がる。

ja: 自摸牌は白になる。一時的。

ja: 次に自模るべき牌が山にある風牌と居場所を交換。風牌がない場合に無益。

ja: ９ヴォルトでない充電できるアイテムが９充電。

ja: 一番最近に現れた槓ドラを選べた手牌また自摸牌と交換。

ja: 選べた筒子を選べた筒子に変更。一時的。

en: Convert a selected Sou into a selected Sou's predecessor [i]temporarily[/i].
ja: 選べた索子を選べた索子の一つ下に変更。一時的。

ja: 自摸じゃないランダムな手牌を赤くする。一時的。

ja: 自摸牌にポッチを埋め込む。永続的。

ja: 選べた萬子を一番遠い老頭牌に変更。一時的。

ja: 自摸牌を＋／ー３変更。一時的。

The Prevalent Wind. Changes every 4 rounds.
Mana. Increases every time a tile is drawn.
ja: マナ。牌を自摸とマナを得る。
牌山の後ろ。普通に自模らない。
